title: HTTP 400 Bad Request
meaning: The server cannot process the request because the request is invalid or malformed.
quickFix: Inspect the request payload, parameter names, required fields, and content type.
details: Compare the request with the service's current API contract.
Validate JSON syntax and required fields.
Check whether a parameter uses the correct data type.
prevention: Validate requests before sending and keep API contracts versioned.

title: HTTP 401 Unauthorized
meaning: The request lacks valid authentication credentials or the credentials are not accepted.
quickFix: Verify the authentication method and obtain a fresh approved credential.
details: Confirm the endpoint and authentication flow.
Check token expiry and audience metadata without exposing the token.
Review identity-provider logs when available.
prevention: Use secure credential storage and controlled rotation.

title: HTTP 403 Forbidden
meaning: The request is understood but access to the resource or operation is not permitted.
quickFix: Identify the effective identity and required permission before changing access.
details: Check role assignments and resource policies.
Look for explicit deny or organizational policy.
Grant only the minimum permission required.
prevention: Use least privilege and periodic access reviews.

title: HTTP 404 Not Found
meaning: The requested resource or endpoint could not be found.
quickFix: Verify the endpoint, resource identifier, API version, and environment.
details: Compare the URL with current documentation.
Check whether the resource exists in the selected account or subscription.
Confirm path parameters.
prevention: Use environment-aware configuration and endpoint tests.

title: HTTP 408 Request Timeout
meaning: The server did not receive a complete request within the allowed time.
quickFix: Retry safely and investigate network and service latency.
details: Check whether the problem is intermittent.
Review client and server timeout settings.
Avoid repeated retries for non-idempotent operations without safeguards.
prevention: Use appropriate timeouts and controlled retry strategies.

title: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests
meaning: The client has sent requests faster than the service currently allows.
quickFix: Respect Retry-After when provided and use exponential backoff.
details: Reduce request frequency.
Cache safe responses where appropriate.
Review client retry logic.
prevention: Implement rate-aware clients, caching, and backoff.

title: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
meaning: The server encountered an unexpected condition while processing the request.
quickFix: Retry if the operation is safe, then inspect service logs or status information.
details: Capture request IDs and timestamps.
Check dependency health.
Review recent deployments or configuration changes.
prevention: Monitoring, testing, controlled deployments, and resilient dependency handling.

title: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway
meaning: A gateway or proxy received an invalid response from an upstream service.
quickFix: Check service health and retry safely if appropriate.
details: Determine whether the error is isolated or widespread.
Inspect proxy and upstream logs when available.
Check DNS and network connectivity.
prevention: Monitor upstream dependencies and configure resilient gateways.

title: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
meaning: The service is temporarily unable to handle the request.
quickFix: Check service status and retry using controlled backoff.
details: Look for maintenance notifications.
Check capacity and dependency health.
Avoid aggressive retries that increase load.
prevention: Capacity planning, health checks, and graceful degradation.

title: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout
meaning: A gateway did not receive a timely response from an upstream service.
quickFix: Check upstream latency and retry safely where supported.
details: Measure request duration.
Check gateway and upstream logs.
Review timeouts across the request chain.
prevention: Performance monitoring and appropriate timeout/retry design.

title: Azure 403 Forbidden
meaning: Azure received the request but the identity or policy is not permitted to perform the operation.
quickFix: Review the effective identity, role assignments, resource policies, and network restrictions.
details: Confirm subscription and resource context.
Check for explicit denies and organizational policy.
Use least privilege when correcting access.
prevention: Centralized RBAC governance and regular access reviews.

title: Azure 401 Unauthorized
meaning: An Azure API or service endpoint rejected the authentication information.
quickFix: Acquire a fresh credential through the approved authentication flow and verify endpoint context.
details: Check issuer, audience, expiry, tenant, and requested scope without exposing secrets.
Review application registration configuration.
prevention: Managed identities and secure secret management where supported.

title: Salesforce API Authentication Error
meaning: A Salesforce integration cannot authenticate successfully.
quickFix: Verify the integration environment and authentication configuration without exposing credentials.
details: Review OAuth flow, connected-app policies, user permissions, and integration logs.
prevention: Managed secrets and controlled token rotation.

title: Power BI Gateway Connection Error
meaning: Power BI Service cannot reach or use the configured data gateway.
quickFix: Check gateway status, host availability, mappings, and credentials.
details: Review gateway cluster status and relevant logs.
Validate source connectivity from the gateway host.

title: Jira Automation Rule Not Triggering
meaning: A Jira automation rule did not execute for the expected event.
quickFix: Review the automation audit log and verify trigger, scope, and conditions.
details: Test with a controlled issue and inspect where execution stops.
prevention: Keep automation rules small and test changes before rollout.
